assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks turned an idea (magic-wavelength trapping of many atoms, Katori) into the most accurate measurement devices ever built, with fractional uncertainty near 1e-18. The discovery sits at the centre of precision physics: redefinition of the second, relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and searches for dark-matter signatures. Originality and lasting impact are clear.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and made the first demonstrations; Jun Ye's group brought the strontium lattice clock to extreme accuracy and coherence. Two names give a clean, defensible configuration. Other groups (for example Lemonde, Hinkley/Ludlow/Oates, Hall as a precursor via the 2005 prize) contributed but are outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature: many independent labs worldwide reproduce and improve the performance, and clock comparisons are routine. Timing is good, with the redefinition of the second under discussion. Prior prizes on frequency combs (2005) and ion clocks (2012) are adjacent but distinct.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views the work as sufficiently distinct from the 2005 and 2012 prizes.
Roles of other early lattice-clock groups are not fully resolved from the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators opened a new class of quantum matter, with protected edge and surface states, from the quantum spin Hall effect predicted in graphene and HgTe to three-dimensional topological insulators observed by ARPES. The concept reshaped condensed-matter physics and links to topological band theory; it follows naturally after the 2016 Nobel Prize on topological phase transitions without duplicating it.
assessment.attribution: Kane (with Mele) supplied the decisive theory; Molenkamp's group gave the first experimental quantum spin Hall observation in HgTe, and Hasan's group the first 3D topological insulator observations. Mele and, outside the supplied names, Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, Fu and Kane, Moore and Balents also made key contributions, so a three-person cut leaves a real credit problem.
assessment.maturity: Mature: roughly two decades of independent confirmation across materials and techniques, and the interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Treatment of Mele and the HgTe theory proposers is unresolved with a three-laureate limit.
Overlap with the separate QAH candidates B004 and B034 means the committee must decide how to scope the topic.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the field of moire quantum materials. A tunable, clean platform for strong correlations is a clear discovery with wide influence, including on fractional Chern insulators and related phases.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the key 2011 prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the 2018 experimental discoveries. This is a natural theory-plus-experiment pairing. Eva Andrei's early STM and transport evidence for the flat-band physics is credited in the list and is a real attribution tension; Cory Dean and others also matter in the wider moire field.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature in observation, as many groups reproduce the phase diagram, but the microscopic pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is still debated. Slightly early, though the discovery itself is secure.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism and the nature of the superconductivity remain contested.
Whether Andrei should be recognised over or alongside Bistritzer and MacDonald is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Measurement of a large theta13 completed the lepton mixing matrix, opened the way to CP-violation searches in neutrinos and constrained the mass ordering programme. It is a clean, precise discovery rather than an interpretation, and it follows the 2015 prize for neutrino oscillations.
assessment.attribution: Daya Bay (Wang, Luk) reported the decisive reactor-disappearance observation at high significance in 2012, alongside RENO and Double Chooz; T2K (Nishikawa) gave the earliest appearance indication in 2011. Large collaborations make individual selection arbitrary, and RENO and Double Chooz leaders are outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature: independent reactor and accelerator experiments agree and the value has been refined for over a decade. Timing is acceptable though not urgent.
uncertainties: Credit split among Daya Bay, RENO, Double Chooz and T2K is contested and unresolved.
The committee may judge it an incremental parameter measurement after the 2015 prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation explains flatness, horizon uniformity and the primordial perturbation spectrum, and its generic predictions of near scale invariance and adiabatic Gaussian perturbations have been confirmed by CMB measurements. It is among the most consequential ideas in cosmology. As a theorist I am cautious, however: the inflaton and the energy scale are unknown and no primordial gravitational-wave signal has been seen.
assessment.attribution: Guth proposed the original scenario, Linde the new and chaotic inflation that made it work, and Mukhanov computed the quantum origin of structure. Starobinsky's earlier model and Sato, Albrecht and Steinhardt, Chibisov, Hawking, Bardeen and others have strong claims; none are in the supplied names, so the configuration is vulnerable.
assessment.maturity: The observational support is for the perturbation spectrum, not for inflation as a mechanism uniquely. The Nobel standard of confirmation is met in part but the theory remains underdetermined; timing is arguable.
uncertainties: Attribution is seriously contested, notably Starobinsky, which the supplied credit cannot resolve.
Whether current evidence confirms inflation itself, as opposed to its spectral predictions, is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The IceCube detection of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos at TeV-PeV energies, followed by evidence for TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane, founded neutrino astronomy. It is a genuine discovery of a new messenger with lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube and its predecessor AMANDA, but the discovery is the work of a large collaboration and is only partly attributable to one person. A single-name list cannot easily form a fair configuration, and Learned, Markov, Reines and the KM3NeT or Baikal pioneers are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Mature in the core detection, confirmed by multiple IceCube analyses; source identification is still developing and independent confirmation from KM3NeT is limited so far.
uncertainties: Single-person credit for a collaboration discovery is difficult to justify.
Source population and production mechanisms remain unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED provided strong coupling of superconducting artificial atoms to microwave resonators, enabling dispersive readout, quantum-state control and today's superconducting quantum processors. Impact on quantum technology and on quantum optics is lasting and large.
assessment.attribution: Blais and collaborators supplied the theory; Wallraff and Schoelkopf demonstrated strong coupling in 2004 and developed the architecture. Girvin, Devoret and Nakamura are also central, and the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum effects in circuits already recognised Clarke, Devoret and Martinis, so the allocation is sensitive.
assessment.maturity: Mature in method with many confirming groups, but a very recent prize in the same area suggests waiting, and large-scale impact is still being established.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 superconducting-circuit prize reduces the case for near-term recognition.
Roles of Girvin, Devoret and Nakamura relative to the credited names are unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions and its experimental realisation made trapped ions the leading platform for high-fidelity quantum computation and simulation. This is a significant conceptual and experimental advance, although it builds on ion-control work honoured in 2012.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the 1995 proposal; Blatt led the principal experimental realisations and scaling. Wineland, Monroe and Kielpinski are also central, and Wineland already holds the 2012 prize, which complicates the case.
assessment.maturity: Mature experimentally, with independent confirmation and commercial systems. The topic overlaps the 2012 prize and the broader quantum-information field, so the timing is uncertain.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize and with the Zoller-Cirac optical-lattice proposals in B041.
Whether the Monroe and Wineland groups should be credited more than Blatt is unresolved.
